title: Live-tweakable parameters: mark a field, tune it in a debug menu while the scene runs, and write the value back to its source literal
description:
Rebuilt 2026-10-25 from content/ENG/ENG-13.json, which held pasted design notes instead of a ticket JSON (committed in 'added tickets', so the board skipped it); the original text is kept at references/ENG-13/original-notes.md.

The idea (a Jonathan Blow-style tuning workflow): mark tuning fields with an annotation (min, max, display name); a debug menu lists the marked fields of the running scene with sliders; changing one applies immediately (the owning scene reloads what depends on it); a Save action rewrites that field's literal in its .java source so the tuned value is kept.

Constraints from the codebase since the notes were written: no runtime reflection over arbitrary classes (the user ruled it out for automation state; prefer the compile-time annotation processors the project already uses for registries); no machine-specific source path (resolve the checkout like REPO_HOME, never a hard-coded C:/... path); static final constants are inlined by javac, so tuned fields cannot be final; the menu is a ControlHint/terminal-driven UI like the rest of the scene controls, reachable from ixdar-cli; the source rewrite goes through a parser (or an exact, refusing match), never a loose regex.
definition-of-done:
1. A field marked tunable shows in the scene's tuning menu and changes the running scene when moved.
2. Save rewrites exactly that literal in the source and refuses (with a message) when it cannot.
3. Works through ixdar-cli as well as the UI; tests for the source rewrite.
testing-plan:
1. mvn test.
2. Tune a value in a scene, save, rebuild, see it kept.
